newsitem.title: UK: Tate & Lyle '96 profits drop 11 pct, dividend up.
newsitem.headline: Tate & Lyle '96 profits drop 11 pct, dividend up.

text.p: Tate & Lyle, the British sugar and starch producer, said on Wednesday full-year 1996 profits fell 11 percent to 276.3 million pounds after an earnings drop of more than 50 percent at U.S. subsidiary Staley.

But Chairman Neil Shaw said other parts of the business made good progress and an ambitious investment programme was continuing. The board recommended a final dividend of 11.7p, bringing the total for the year to 17.0p, an increase of six percent.

"The investments we are making in international markets, together with the significant improvements we have undertaken in our existing plants will, we are sure, contribute to our continuing long-term growth," Shaw told shareholders.
He said the drop in pre-tax profits was only the second in 18 years. The profits figure was within analysts' forecasts which ranged from 270 to 285 million pounds.
Staley, the company's major U.S. sweetener and starch producer, was hit by a record increase in maize costs which Shaw said could not be passed on to consumers.

But he said group profits reached the level achieved in 1994, the second highest ever, and he singled out progress in U.S. cane sugar operations. Tate & Lyle shares rose 3-1/2p to 473-1/2p by 0828 GMT.
